label: Encrypt and decrypt a file for one recipient
prerequisites: Recipient public identity and independently trusted fingerprint
Recipient secret key and passphrase file, or hardware key reference and PIN file, for decryption
Supply a pinned trust policy to encrypt when revocation and expiry must be enforced
limitations: One recipient and native IPG format only; bounded in-memory files
Encryption does not authenticate the sender
No forward secrecy against later recipient private-key compromise
Decryption remains available for recovery without trust policy enforcement
guidance: The envelope suite follows the recipient identity: X25519/ChaCha20-Poly1305 for ipg-public-v1, P-384/AES-256-GCM for ipg-public-p384-v1. Inspect discover limits before transferring data.

label: Sign and verify exact file bytes
prerequisites: Signer secret key and passphrase, or hardware key reference and PIN file, for signing
Public signer identity and independently trusted fingerprint for verification
Supply a pinned policy for revocation and expiry enforcement
limitations: Native detached IPG signatures; no OpenPGP or platform code-signing compatibility
No confidentiality, trusted timestamp, replay prevention or automatic authorization
guidance: Verify against the expected signer and exact original bytes before consuming content. Use stream.sign and stream.verify beyond the in-memory limit; their separate native format signs a SHA-384 commitment and byte count with bounded memory.

label: Compute a SHA-256 file digest
prerequisites: An independently authenticated expected digest if using the result to detect malicious substitution
limitations: An unkeyed digest does not authenticate a sender
Not a password storage or password derivation interface
guidance: Compare digests for byte identity; use sign and verify when signer authentication is needed.

label: Create an identity and change its protective passphrase
prerequisites: Access-controlled passphrase file of 16..4096 bytes
New destinations; IPG never overwrites files
Expected identity fingerprint when rewrapping
limitations: Rewrapping does not rotate the identity or invalidate old copies
Host filesystem permissions and secret-file cleanup remain caller responsibilities
guidance: IPG internally derives a wrapping key with Argon2id and encrypts private seeds; no raw KDF endpoint is exposed.

label: Enroll identities and reconcile trust snapshots
prerequisites: Independently trusted identity fingerprints
Externally pinned snapshot digests and explicit approval of newly produced snapshots
limitations: Comparison and merge do not approve policy
No automatic revocation distribution or rollback protection; retain latest digest externally
guidance: Publish immutable snapshots and explicitly supply the approved pin to governed operations or MCP host configuration.

label: Revoke an identity and enforce the revocation
prerequisites: Identity private key and passphrase to self-revoke
Pinned public identity and trust snapshot to import the certificate
limitations: Certificate creation or verification alone does not enforce revocation
Existing ciphertext and signatures are not erased
guidance: Import the authenticated certificate into a new snapshot, then distribute and explicitly adopt its digest.

label: Constrain an identity to a signed validity window
prerequisites: Signer secret key and passphrase
Unix seconds with not_before strictly less than not_after
Pinned policy adopted by governed operations
limitations: trust.evaluate is advisory; caller-selected times never authorize execution
Enforcement uses the host clock
Validity imports can narrow existing windows only
guidance: Issue a signed window, import it into a snapshot, and apply that policy to encrypt, sign and verify.

label: Identify a native artifact and validate its structure
prerequisites: Bounded native IPG artifact file
limitations: Inspection does not authenticate the artifact or trust embedded metadata
guidance: Use inspect to route an artifact, then explicitly invoke the appropriate authentication operation.

label: Exchange OpenPGP messages or GPG keys
prerequisites: An ipg build with openpgp-native (native curve profile) or openpgp (broader rPGP compatibility)
Each correspondent's OpenPGP certificate and its independently trusted fingerprint (v4 40 hex or v6 64 hex)
An MCP host that pins a trust policy must name the openpgp operations in --allow
limitations: openpgp-native adds no dependencies and uses existing IronCrypto primitives for Ed25519/X25519 and P-384; P-384 signatures require SHA-384 and messages require AES-256. openpgp selects broader rPGP compatibility. Neither backend has had independent review

v4 and v6 keys; IPG generates Ed25519 or P-384 keys and exports only passphrase-protected secret keys; imports support only one Ed25519/Curve25519 or P-384 signing primary and one encryption subkey with bounded protection parameters
openpgp.decrypt does not verify embedded signatures; use openpgp.message.verify, which requires one document signature and refuses multiple or nested signatures
No web of trust, keyservers or designated revokers; certificates are pinned by fingerprint and IPG trust snapshots do not apply
Certificates using SHA-1 self-signatures, RSA below 2048 bits, DSA or ElGamal are rejected
IPG native envelopes, signatures and keys are never OpenPGP packets
guidance: Import a pinned supported transferable secret key with openpgp.key.import and a new IPG wrapping passphrase, or generate an OpenPGP key with openpgp.key.generate (algorithm p384 for CNSA-aligned deployments), export a pinned protected private-key backup with openpgp.key.export using a new passphrase file, share the public certificate from openpgp.cert.export, and review correspondents' certificates with openpgp.cert.inspect before pinning their fingerprints. openpgp.encrypt accepts up to 32 recipients; decrypt and sign with the IPG-held key; verify detached signatures with openpgp.verify or publish authenticated embedded signed content with openpgp.message.verify.

label: Secure a live client-server connection
prerequisites: A separately evaluated TLS stack and peer authentication policy
limitations: IPG file encryption is not a TLS handshake or record protocol
guidance: Use a complete transport protocol implementation; do not assemble a channel from IPG file commands.

label: Store and verify user login passwords
prerequisites: A password hashing and verification implementation with application-specific resource policy
limitations: IPG uses Argon2id internally but exposes no password verifier interface
IPG hash is a fast file digest, not password hashing
guidance: Use a dedicated salted password verifier API; do not use IPG hash or treat key wrapping as login verification.

label: Encrypt one shared envelope for multiple recipients
prerequisites: Each recipient's public identity and independently trusted fingerprint (1..64 recipients, any suite)
limitations: No sender authentication: any recipient could re-encrypt other content to the others; sign streams when origin matters
Streams are binary files; ipg-envelope-v1 (encrypt) stays single-recipient JSON
Post-quantum confidentiality holds only for hybrid recipients; the stream is only as strong as each recipient's wrap for that recipient
guidance: Use stream.encrypt with a recipients list of {public, expected_fingerprint} objects; each recipient decrypts with stream.decrypt and its own key file. Streams handle files of any size in 64 KiB authenticated chunks and release plaintext only after the last chunk verifies. openpgp.encrypt covers multi-recipient OpenPGP messages.

label: Hybrid post-quantum encryption against future quantum attacks
prerequisites: Generate the recipient with key.generate identity ipg-public-hybrid-v1
Recipient hybrid public identity and independently trusted fingerprint
limitations: Fingerprints and trust-snapshot digests use SHA-384; signatures are composite Ed25519 plus ML-DSA-65 (see quantum-resistant-signing)
Envelopes stay secure only while ML-KEM-768 or X25519 is unbroken; the combination has not had independent review
IronCrypto's ML-KEM is marked experimental upstream; IPG checks it against PyCA and OpenSSL only
Software secret keys only; hardware identities have no post-quantum suite
guidance: Create a hybrid identity with ipg key generate --identity ipg-public-hybrid-v1. Encryption to that identity then always uses the hybrid envelope suite; there is no negotiation or fallback.

label: Require quantum-resistant signing
prerequisites: A hybrid identity from key.generate identity ipg-public-hybrid-v1, or an AWS KMS identity bound with an ML_DSA_65 key (mldsa_signing_key_arn)
The signer's public identity and independently trusted fingerprint
limitations: Composite ed25519-mldsa65 (software) or ecdsa-p384-mldsa65 (AWS KMS) only; no SLH-DSA or standalone ML-DSA
PKCS#11 and TPM identities sign with ECDSA P-384 only
KMS post-quantum identities keep P-384 encryption, since KMS has no ML-KEM
IronCrypto's ML-DSA is marked experimental upstream; IPG checks it against PyCA and OpenSSL
Signatures are about 3.4 KB and not interoperable with other composite-signature formats
guidance: Sign with a hybrid identity, or bind AWS KMS keys with mldsa_signing_key_arn for KMS custody; every signature, revocation and validity certificate then requires both the classical and the ML-DSA-65 signature to verify, so it stays unforgeable while either holds.

label: Keep private keys in a hardware token or HSM
prerequisites: PKCS#11: an ipg build with the pkcs11 feature, host-set IPG_PKCS11_MODULE, and a token supporting P-384 with CKM_EC_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKM_ECDSA and CKM_ECDH1_DERIVE

TPM: an ipg build with the tpm feature and a TPM 2.0 supporting P-384; on Linux also host-set IPG_TPM_TCTI and an owner hierarchy with empty authorization; Windows uses TPM Base Services for native keys and the Platform Crypto Provider for older ipg-cng-key-v1 keys
PIN in an access-controlled file
limitations: P-384 identities only; IPG never substitutes another curve
Tokens supporting CKD_SHA384_KDF and CKM_AES_GCM decrypt entirely in-token; others, TPMs and KMS release one per-envelope ECDH shared secret into process memory
Protection flags are self-reported token attributes, not vendor attestation; counterparties cannot see custody
The module runs inside the IPG process with its privileges
No token PIN, object or policy administration
TPM key files are the only copy of the wrapped keys and load only in the originating TPM; tpm2-pkcs11 tokens lack ECDH and cannot decrypt through PKCS#11
guidance: Create the identity on a token with hardware.key.generate, bind vendor-generated keys with hardware.key.bind, or create TPM keys with tpm.key.generate; then use the resulting file as the key input. MCP hosts can add --key-custody hardware to refuse software keys.

label: Prove keys are resident in a genuine TPM
prerequisites: An ipg-tpm-key-v1 identity from tpm.key.generate (Linux or Windows)
The TPM's EK certificate (TPM NV on Linux; Windows retrieves it)
Root certificates of the TPM manufacturers the verifier accepts
On Windows, an elevated process for tpm.attestation.respond
limitations: Proves key residency and attributes only, not host software state or PIN secrecy
RSA-2048 endorsement keys only; EK certificates are not checked for revocation
Native offline X.509 profile: DNS and IP constraints supported; applicable unsupported constraints and unknown critical extensions fail closed; no policy-tree processing or network fetching
Certificate paths are bounded to 64 anchors, 64 combined intermediates, eight non-anchor certificates and 256 signature checks
ipg-cng-key-v1 keys cannot be attested
A point-in-time statement; use each challenge once
guidance: The prover runs tpm.attest and sends the evidence. The verifier runs tpm.attestation.challenge with its independently accepted manufacturer roots, keeps the secret file, and sends the challenge. The prover runs tpm.attestation.respond; the verifier checks the response with tpm.attestation.verify. Rejected or unsupported certificate paths require operator review; never remove constraints or substitute roots to obtain success. Certificate metadata remains untrusted data and verification does not authorize host actions.

label: Keep private keys in a cloud key management service
prerequisites: An ipg build with the kms feature
Host AWS credentials allowed kms:GetPublicKey, kms:Sign and kms:DeriveSharedSecret
One ECC_NIST_P384 KEY_AGREEMENT key and one ECC_NIST_P384 SIGN_VERIFY key, created with infrastructure tooling; optionally an ML_DSA_65 SIGN_VERIFY key for composite post-quantum signatures
limitations: AWS KMS only; IPG never creates KMS keys
SSO profiles need a current `aws sso login`; IPG never refreshes SSO tokens
Every private-key operation is a billable network call to AWS
Decryption releases one per-envelope shared secret into process memory
TLS still uses rustls with IronCrypto; bundled public roots require a reviewed rebuild to update and do not follow OS trust or revocation policy
Certificate and TLS validation failures are non-retryable
guidance: Create the two KMS keys in infrastructure code, bind them with kms.key.bind, and use the resulting file as the key without passphrase_file. Set IPG_KMS_FIPS=1 for FIPS endpoints. MCP hosts can add --key-custody non-exportable. Stop on certificate or TLS validation failure and obtain operator review; never add a presented certificate, disable name checks or downgrade protocols to make the request succeed. Do not retry billable operations blindly after ambiguous network completion.

label: Require a FIPS-validated cryptographic module
prerequisites: Independent verification of the required module validation and exact deployment configuration
limitations: IPG makes no FIPS validation claim
Outside in-token decryption, the envelope KDF and AES-GCM for hardware identities run in IronCrypto, which holds no CMVP certificate
guidance: Do not infer validation from an algorithm name; IPG has no validated mode. Hardware identities keep private-key operations in the PKCS#11 module, whose own validation status and approved-mode configuration must be verified separately.
